views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the G20 90-day window open and treat the January high-level talks as a purchase-and-process negotiation, not a structural surrender. Offer a large, verifiable increase in US agricultural, energy, and manufactured-goods imports to give Washington a face-saving path to leave List 3 at 10% past the March deadline, while refusing irreversible changes to industrial policy, SOE governance, or Made-in-China 2025. Do not add tariffs or further high-profile detentions during the truce; those would likely collapse talks and trigger the already-scheduled 10-to-25% hike on ~$200B of Chinese exports.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Combined US Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B (Lists 1–3), China’s matching retaliation tops out around $60B plus the earlier $3B 232 package, and the Jan 1, 2019 List-3 hike to 25% is only suspended—not cancelled—pending a deal (timeline 2018-09-24, 2018-12-01). Firm-level targeting is real and escalating: the April 2018 ZTE denial order, Meng Wanzhou’s 1 Dec arrest, the 10 Dec detention of Kovrig and Spavor, and the 28 Jan DOJ fraud/sanctions/trade-secret charges plus formal extradition request all hit a national-champion tech champion (timeline 2018-04-16, 2018-12-01, 2018-12-10, 2019-01-28). Official 2018 GDP slowed to 6.6% and Q4 to 6.4%—a three-decade low—with December exports contracting as tariffs began to bite, auto sales weak, and NBS acknowledging rising downward pressure. That maps near the CHN +0.5 anchor (export sectors, Huawei, unemployment risk in export hubs) but not +1.0: industrial production was still +5.7% y/y in December, FX reserves held ~$3.11T, the yuan strengthened from ~6.97 in late October to 6.71 on 30 Jan, and high-level talks are live (Lighthizer/Mnuchin, 30 Jan) with purchase commitments on the table and structural IP/tech-transfer still unresolved (timeline 2019-01-07, 2019-01-30). Action should stay near zero because a May-2018 purchases-only truce already collapsed when the White House reopened 301, Lighthizer is publicly demanding verification and structural change rather than another empty soybean pledge, and further Chinese escalation (new tariffs or more hostage diplomacy) would give hawks the pretext to let the March hike proceed. Negotiation—purchases plus process, no core concession—is the stance that uses US market-sensitivity (UMCSENT 91.2, US goods exports to China down ~27% in the window) without trading away the industrial model the Party will not give up.
key_factors: US Section 301 already covers ~$250B; List 3 10%→25% hike is only suspended through the G20 90-day window
Huawei/Meng criminal track (28 Jan DOJ charges + extradition) plus ZTE precedent is firm-level tech coercion, not just tariffs
2018 GDP 6.6% / Q4 6.4% three-decade low and December export contraction raise the domestic cost of a failed truce
Purchase commitments are the only live landing zone; structural IP/tech-transfer/enforcement remain open and were the reason the May 2018 truce collapsed
Macro buffers still intact (reserves ~$3.11T, CNY stronger at 6.71, IP still expanding) so this is high threat, not a financial emergency
Further Chinese escalation during talks would likely trigger the March hike and US decoupling talk rather than extract leverage

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
G20 Buenos Aires dinner: Trump and Xi agree to a 90-day negotiation window. Planned Jan 1, 2019 hike of List 3 from 10% to 25% is suspended. Same day: Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou.
US DOJ unseals fraud and sanctions-related charges against Huawei and Meng; US formally requests Meng's extradition from Canada.
Lighthizer and Mnuchin in Beijing for high-level talks. Purchase commitments discussed; enforcement and structural IP/tech-transfer issues unresolved.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to significantly increase purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is on hold.
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
China total reserves excluding gold latest ~$3.107T (2019-01), essentially unchanged over the window.
CNY/USD strengthened to 6.7115 on 2019-01-30 from ~6.97 peak in late October after the G20 truce.
China SA merchandise exports fell from $216.3B (2018-09) to $196.9B (2018-12) before a partial rebound to $211.0B (2019-01).
US goods exports to mainland China down ~27% over the window to $7.1B in January 2019, showing US export pain China can use in talks.
China's economy grew 6.6% in 2018, the lowest pace in 28 years; Q4 growth 6.4%. NBS said the trade dispute affected the domestic economy but the impact was manageable.
Jan 7–9 Beijing talks focused on structural changes and China's pledge to purchase a substantial amount of US goods; little indication of progress on larger structural changes.
DOJ unsealed criminal charges against Huawei and requested Meng's extradition; White House said the charges are a totally separate process from trade talks.
